3 خالسهُ الشَّىْءَ , (A, TA, *) inf. n. مُخَالَسَةٌ and خِلَاسٌ, (TA,) [He contended with him in a mutual endeavouring to seize, or carry off, the thing by force; or to take it at an opportunity, with deceit, guile, or circumvention; or to take it hastily and openly; or to snatch it at unawares: see 1 and 6.] A poet says, [app. using the verb tropically,] “نَظَرْتُ إِلَىمَىٍّ خِلَاسًا عَشِيَّةً
عَلَى عَجَلٍ وَ ٱلْكَاشِحُونَ حُضُورُ
” [I looked at Mei, vying with her in snatching glances, in the evening, in haste, while the secret enemies were present]. (Th, TA.) ―
-b2- See also 1.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
